name: Sharjah Heritage Museum
short: Emirati life, customs and crafts in the restored home of a pearl merchant.
description: The Sharjah Heritage Museum sits in the old town, inside the Heart of Sharjah heritage district. It occupies the restored home of Saeed Al Taweel Al Shamsi, a pearl merchant, and first opened in 2005 before reopening in 2012. Six themed galleries cover Sharjah's landscape, daily life and customs, celebrations such as Ramadan and Eid, traditional livelihoods like pearl diving and date farming, traditional knowledge of the desert and the sky, and oral traditions including poems, proverbs and legends.

name: Al Noor Mosque
short: An Ottoman-style mosque on the Khalid Lagoon, open to visitors for guided tours.
description: Inspired by the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) in Istanbul, Al Noor Mosque was completed in 2005 on the Buhaira Corniche overlooking the Khalid Lagoon. It has 34 domes and two 52-metre minarets, and can hold around 2,200 worshippers. The mosque is open to visitors, and it is especially striking at night when it is lit up. Modest dress is required.

name: Museum of Islamic Civilization
short: Over 5,000 artefacts covering Islamic science, art and faith under a golden dome.
description: Housed in the former Souq Al Majarrah on the Corniche, the Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilization opened in 2008 and displays more than 5,000 artefacts from across the Islamic world. Its galleries cover the Islamic faith, science and technology, and Islamic art, from early Arabia through the Umayyad, Mamluk and Ottoman eras. Don't miss the gilded central dome, decorated inside with a mosaic of the night sky and the 12 signs of the zodiac.

name: Sharjah Art Museum
short: One of the region's largest art museums, with Orientalist and modern Arab art.
description: Sharjah Art Museum opened in 1997 during the 3rd Sharjah International Arts Biennial and is one of the largest art museums in the Gulf. Its galleries are spread over two floors. A permanent gallery shows highlights from Sheikh Sultan bin Muhammad Al Qasimi's Orientalist collection, alongside modern and contemporary works by artists from the UAE and the wider Arab world, and regular temporary exhibitions.

name: Al Hisn Sharjah
short: The 1820s fort that was once home to the ruling family, now a museum.
description: Al Hisn Sharjah was built around 1820 from coral stone and was the seat of the ruling Al Qasimi family. Most of the fort was demolished in 1969. Sheikh Sultan bin Muhammad Al Qasimi kept its original doors, including the main Al Sabah gate, and later had the fort rebuilt from historical photographs; it reopened as a museum in 2015. Inside, two levels of galleries cover the fort's history and restoration, the Al Qawasim family, the Mahloussa prison and the Al Kabis Tower.
location: Al Hisn Avenue, Heart of Sharjah

name: Al Majaz Waterfront
short: Lagoon-side parks, dancing fountains and cafés, best at sunset.
description: Al Majaz Waterfront stretches along the Khalid Lagoon with gardens, walking and cycling paths, a zero-depth splash park, an art and sculpture park, and a row of restaurants and cafés. In the evening the Sharjah Fountain, 220 metres wide with jets reaching up to 100 metres, puts on music, light and laser shows over the water.
